# OpenSanctions Sanctions, PEP & Watchlist Data Extractor

Stream entities from OpenSanctions, the open-data project that consolidates 400+ government and watchdog sources into one structured feed. Pull persons, companies, vessels and other entities from a specific list — OFAC SDN, UN Security Council, EU sanctions, politically exposed persons, debarment registers, wanted lists and more — or list every available dataset with its size, publisher and coverage. No API key required.

## What this actor does

- **Two modes:** `getDatasetEntities` streams the entities of one chosen dataset; `listDatasets` returns metadata for every dataset in the OpenSanctions index
- **400+ datasets** — pick a well-known source (OFAC SDN, UN sanctions, INTERPOL Red Notices, Wikidata PEPs) or a consolidated collection (all sanctions, all PEPs, all debarment lists), or type any dataset name to override the dropdown
- **Entity-type and topic filters** — narrow a stream to persons, organizations, companies or vessels, and to a topic like `sanction`, `role.pep`, or `crime.fraud` (topics are hierarchical, so `crime` also matches `crime.fin`, `crime.fraud`, etc.)
- **Dataset discovery** — `listDatasets` can be restricted to sources, collections, or external enrichment datasets, sorted by entity count
- **Empty fields are omitted** — a record only carries the attributes OpenSanctions published for that entity or dataset

## Output per entity (mode `getDatasetEntities`)

- `id` — OpenSanctions entity ID
- `schema` — FollowTheMoney type, e.g. `Person`, `Company`, `Vessel`
- `name`, `aliases[]`
- `countries[]`, `nationalities[]`
- `topics[]` — e.g. `sanction`, `role.pep`, `crime.fin`
- `datasets[]` — every OpenSanctions dataset this entity appears in
- `birthDate`, `gender`, `positions[]`
- `registrationNumber`, `addresses[]`, `website`
- `programs[]` — sanctions program IDs, when listed
- `referenceUrl` — the original source document, when OpenSanctions provides one
- `firstSeen`, `lastSeen` — when OpenSanctions first/last observed this entity
- `isTarget` — `true` when OpenSanctions flags this as a directly targeted entity (not just a related party)
- `sourceUrl` — the entity's OpenSanctions profile page
- `recordType: "entity"`, `scrapedAt`

## Output per dataset (mode `listDatasets`)

- `name` — dataset identifier, e.g. `us_ofac_sdn`
- `title`, `summary`, `datasetType` — `source`, `collection`, or `external`
- `entityCount`, `thingCount`, `targetCount` — when greater than zero
- `publisher`, `publisherCountry`
- `tags[]`, `updateFrequency`
- `sourceUrl` — the publisher's own source page
- `pageUrl` — the dataset's OpenSanctions page
- `updatedAt`, `entitiesUrl` — direct link to the dataset's bulk entities file
- `recordType: "dataset"`, `scrapedAt`

## Error records

When the dataset index can't be downloaded, a `dataset`/`datasetName` doesn't match a known dataset, a dataset has no downloadable bulk entities file, or streaming a dataset's entities fails, the actor pushes one record instead of entity/dataset records:

- `recordType: "error"`
- `error` — a short error code, e.g. `unknown_dataset`, `no_bulk_resource`, `download_failed`, `index_unavailable`
- `message` — a human-readable explanation
- `input` — the dataset name or value that triggered the error, when applicable
- `sourceUrl` — the OpenSanctions URL the actor was trying to reach

## Input

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | string | `getDatasetEntities` | `getDatasetEntities` or `listDatasets` |
| `dataset` | string | `us_ofac_sdn` | Dataset to stream, from the curated dropdown (mode `getDatasetEntities`) |
| `datasetName` | string | – | Advanced override: any dataset name or OpenSanctions dataset URL, bypassing the dropdown |
| `schema` | string | `Any` | Entity type filter: `Any` / `Person` / `Organization` / `Company` / `LegalEntity` / `Vessel` / `Address` |
| `topic` | string | `any` | Topic filter, e.g. `sanction`, `role.pep`, `crime.fraud`, `debarment`, `wanted` |
| `datasetType` | string | `all` | Restrict `listDatasets` to `source` / `collection` / `external` |
| `maxItems` | int | `100` | Hard cap on emitted records (1–10000) |

### Example: stream US OFAC SDN persons

```json
{
  "mode": "getDatasetEntities",
  "dataset": "us_ofac_sdn",
  "schema": "Person",
  "maxItems": 500
}
```

### Example: politically exposed persons, worldwide collection

```json
{
  "mode": "getDatasetEntities",
  "dataset": "peps",
  "topic": "role.pep",
  "maxItems": 1000
}
```

### Example: look up a dataset by name override

```json
{
  "mode": "getDatasetEntities",
  "datasetName": "gb_hmt_sanctions",
  "maxItems": 200
}
```

### Example: list every PEP and sanctions collection

```json
{
  "mode": "listDatasets",
  "datasetType": "collection",
  "maxItems": 50
}
```

## Use cases

- **AML/KYC screening** — pull a sanctions or PEP list to check against your own customer or counterparty data
- **Vendor and third-party due diligence** — screen suppliers against debarment and wanted lists
- **Compliance monitoring** — stream a specific list on a schedule to catch newly added entities
- **Research and journalism** — explore a government watchlist's full entity set with names, aliases, and source links
- **Dataset discovery** — use `listDatasets` to find which of OpenSanctions' 400+ lists covers a country or topic you care about

## FAQ

**Do I need an API key?**
No. OpenSanctions publishes its bulk data for free; this actor streams it directly.

**What's the difference between a "source" and a "collection"?**
A source is one government or watchdog's own list (e.g. `us_ofac_sdn`). A collection groups multiple sources together (e.g. `peps` combines every PEP source OpenSanctions tracks). Use `datasetType` in `listDatasets` to tell them apart.

**How do I find a dataset I don't see in the dropdown?**
Run `mode=listDatasets` first to browse all 400+ names, then pass the one you want in `datasetName` (which also accepts a pasted OpenSanctions dataset page URL).

**Why are some entities missing fields like `birthDate` or `registrationNumber`?**
Those fields are specific to persons or companies respectively, and only appear when the source document actually included them. Fields are omitted rather than returned as `null`.

**What does `isTarget` mean?**
OpenSanctions distinguishes entities that are directly named by a sanctions program or watchlist (`isTarget: true`) from related entities it links in for context, like an associate or a shared address, which don't carry that flag.

**How fresh is the data?**
As fresh as OpenSanctions' own bulk export for that dataset — `updatedAt` on a dataset record (from `listDatasets`) tells you when it was last refreshed upstream.

**Is this affiliated with OpenSanctions?**
No. This is an independent third-party actor built on OpenSanctions' public bulk data; it is not affiliated with or endorsed by OpenSanctions.

**Is this a substitute for a licensed compliance screening tool?**
No. This actor streams OpenSanctions' free, open data as-is. For regulated compliance workflows, review OpenSanctions' own licensing terms and consider whether a paid, SLA-backed data source better fits your legal obligations.
